messages:
maria: Hey folks — ran into a repeatable crash in the Python SDK when the server replies with an empty charset in Content-Type. stack shows JSON decode failure in our error parsing path.

kevin: Oof. Can you drop the stack and a minimal repro?

maria: Minimal repro (sync) below and the response headers I saw.

```
# minimal repro (sync)
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
# server returns 400 with headers: {"Content-Type": "application/json; charset=\"\""}
resp = c._session.request("POST", "https://internal.test/errors", json={"x":1})
# client raises JSONDecodeError inside error parsing
# stack: client.py:342 _raise_for_status -> _parse_error -> json.loads(resp.text)
```

maria: Important detail: the raw bytes of the response are valid JSON. The issue is httpx/requests exposes resp.text which attempts to decode using the charset token; when charset is explicitly the empty string decoding blows up and resp.text is unreliable. That leads to json.loads(resp.text) raising JSONDecodeError even though resp.content is valid.

julia: Yep, same class as the earlier non-utf8 body bug. Quick mitigation: stop trusting resp.text when charset is missing/empty. Strategy: 1) try resp.json() (httpx) first inside try/except; 2) if it errors, fallback to resp.content.decode('utf-8', errors='replace') and json.loads that; 3) on any final failure attach a raw_body str and headers to the ClientError so callers can inspect.

kevin: Proposed concrete changes: 
- Update _parse_error to detect json-like Content-Type and prefer resp.json() in a try/except.
- If that fails, do json.loads(resp.content.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')).
- Always set error.raw_body = resp.content.decode('utf-8', errors='replace') if parsing fails; also set error.headers = dict(resp.headers).
- Add raw_body: Optional[str] and headers: Optional[Dict[str,str>] to ClientError dataclass and mirror in AsyncClientError for parity.
- Preserve original JSONDecodeError as __cause__ of the thrown exception so Sentry still shows the underlying trace.
- Add unit tests that exercise: empty charset, missing charset, non-utf8 bytes, and httpx raising on resp.json().

maria: I can attach a failing curl + tiny Flask mock. Will run against CI once PR is up.

julia: Add an async parity test too — we had a gap where AsyncClientError typing lacked the raw_body attribute which made mypy/integration tests fail previously.

kevin: I'll open the PR. Notes for the PR: update stubs (.pyi) for exception fields, add mypy unit tests, and a short changelog entry: "sdk: preserve raw error bodies for malformed Content-Type and add parity between sync/async exceptions". Also include test that asserts error.__cause__ is instance of JSONDecodeError when appropriate.

ci-bot: queued: unit, mypy, integration for branch kevin/sdk-exc-rawbody-null-charset

maria: Quick question — should the exception include the original resp.status_code and url? Might help triage.

julia: Yes, add status_code and request_url to the error payload too (we already put status_code in some places but not always for 4xx parsing failures). Keep the surface small; only str/int fields.

kevin: adding TODOs in PR description. Implementation plan: small change in client._raise_for_status -> call _parse_error which returns a typed Problem dict or raises ClientError. We'll keep that internal but ensure the raised ClientError has these string fields: message, status_code, raw_body, headers, request_url. Update serialization in exceptions tests.

maria: sounds great. I'll run manual e2e against our mock and post results. Please ping me on PR. :thumbsup:

julia: One gotcha — ensure tests don't accidentally rely on resp.json() throwing a simple JSONDecodeError. httpx sometimes raises httpx.DecodingError or ValueError depending on path. Test should accept any exception as __cause__ and assert cause.__class__.__name__ in ("JSONDecodeError", "DecodingError", "ValueError").

kevin: good call. I'll make tests flexible. Also will add a tiny fixture that yields bytes bodies with weird charset header permutations.

maria: Thanks both. This should finally stop noisy crash reports where the body is perfectly fine but parsing blew up.

julia: Nice. After PR merges, we should add a short note to the DX onboarding checklist about best-effort body preservation to help support reproduce errors in customer environments.

kevin: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234 — includes code + tests + changelog. cc @maria @julia

ci-bot: build/test pipeline started for PR 1234 (unit, integration, mypy).

maria: tested locally against flask mock. All green for sync and async. Leaving a couple comments on PR about test cleanup.

kevin: responded to comments and addressed mypy fail on AsyncClientError stub. Will re-run CI.

ci-bot: PR 1234 CI green and merged.

maria: awesome — thanks! :clap:

julia: great iteration. closing thread.
